title: Launch brief (draft): Hosted API overload protection (circuit breakers + load shedding)
body:
Last updated: 2026-01-09 (Nikhil)

Audience
- Product (Hosted API), SRE/Reliability, Support/CS, DevEx/Docs, SDK owners, Sales/SE (for reliability conversations)

Summary
We are rolling out “Hosted circuit breakers + load shedding” to prevent cascading failures during overload and to make customer behavior predictable when capacity is constrained. The customer-visible impact is primarily:
- More consistent overload responses (primarily 429/503) instead of mixed 5xx/timeouts.
- Clear, actionable retry guidance via Retry-After and stable error codes.
- Fewer tail-latency collapses and fewer Sev1/Sev2 incidents during traffic spikes.

This is a reliability feature that changes failure modes. It is not a new quota/rate limit system, but customers will observe more early rejections rather than hanging requests.

Goals for launch
1) Customer experience: predictable, documented overload behavior and retry guidance.
2) Platform stability: shed early, bounded queues, protect routing/control plane responsiveness.
3) Trust: consistent messaging across docs, SDKs, support, and status updates.

What’s changing (customer-facing)
1) Error semantics during overload
- Previously: overload often surfaced as timeouts, ambiguous 500/502/503, streaming disconnects without clear reason.
- Now: when the platform is saturated, requests may be rejected earlier with stable error shapes and headers.

Expected patterns:
- HTTP 429: “too many requests” / admission control / fairness protection at the edge.
- HTTP 503: “service unavailable” / capacity brownout or breaker-open for a model/region/tier.
- Retry-After header: present when a retry is recommended; value is seconds.
- Redwood-specific overload reason codes in the error payload (and mapped into OpenAI-compatible error objects where applicable).

2) Retry guidance
- Customers should respect Retry-After when provided.
- When Retry-After is not present, use exponential backoff with jitter; avoid tight loops.
- If customers have internal retries enabled (SDK + application + gateway), they should ensure they do not stack retries (common cause of retry storms).

3) Changelog / docs
- We will add a public docs section describing:
  - Overload errors (429/503) and what they mean
  - Retry patterns (including jitter) and how to handle streaming
  - Differences between Hosted vs Dedicated behavior

Non-goals / what’s explicitly NOT changing
- Not replacing quotas/rate limiting. Those systems remain.
- Not promising that overload events won’t happen; we are making them safer and clearer.
- Not adding customer-specific bespoke overload logic; we support configuration/policy primitives only.

Customer messaging principles (reviewed w/ SRE)
- Be transparent that overload shedding may occur under extreme spikes.
- Emphasize the benefit: clearer errors + fewer timeouts + better overall uptime and latency under stress.
- Provide actionable client behavior: backoff/jitter, concurrency caps, respect Retry-After, consider reducing max_tokens or prompt sizes.
- Avoid implying “infinite scale” or “no limits.” Avoid “we fixed all 503s.”

Recommended wording snippets
Short description (1–2 sentences)
“Redwood Hosted now includes layered overload protection (circuit breakers and load shedding) to prevent cascading failures during traffic spikes. When capacity is constrained, requests fail fast with consistent 429/503 responses, stable error codes, and Retry-After guidance instead of timeouts.”

Support macro (customer ticket reply)
“Your errors appear consistent with overload protection activating for the requested model/region. Please respect the Retry-After header when present and ensure your client uses exponential backoff with jitter (tight retry loops can amplify load). If you share request IDs and timestamps, we can confirm the overload reason code and suggest mitigation (lower concurrency, reduce max_tokens, or consider Dedicated capacity for sustained spikes).”

If asked “are we being rate limited?”
“Not necessarily. Rate limits and quotas are separate. Under extreme platform load, Redwood may shed requests to protect overall system stability; these responses will include an overload reason code and often a Retry-After header.”

If asked “do these errors count against usage/billing?”
- Proposed customer-facing stance (needs final signoff with Billing/Quotas alignment: Cole Summers):
  - Requests rejected at the edge before inference do not consume tokens and are not billed.
  - If a request starts streaming and then disconnects due to overload, billed behavior should match existing policy (today: we bill tokens actually generated; if nothing generated, no token charge). Confirm final wording before publishing.

Rollout plan (staged)
We are rolling out behind feature flags, by region and model class.

Stage 0: Internal readiness (complete/ongoing)
- SDK error objects expose overload codes + Retry-After cleanly.
- Docs drafts reviewed by DevEx + Support.
- Dashboard and alerting in place to verify we’re shedding rather than failing internally.

Stage 1: Canary (Hosted only)
- Region: us-east
- Scope: 1–2 high-traffic models
- Duration: ~1 week (extend if we observe regressions)
- Success criteria:
  - Reduced p99 latency collapse during synthetic and organic spikes
  - Overload response mix shifts from timeouts/5xx to 429/503 with reason codes
  - No sustained breaker flapping; stable cooldown behavior
  - Support ticket volume stable (or improved clarity when tickets occur)

Stage 2: Expand coverage (Hosted)
- Add additional models in us-east; then add 1–2 more regions
- Validate:
  - Retry-After values correlate with observed recovery times
  - No regressions for streaming reliability
  - No tenant starvation (edge fairness behaving correctly)

Stage 3: General availability behavior for Hosted
- Enabled by default for Hosted routes/models, with documented behavior
- Dedicated alignment: Dedicated remains predictable; load shedding semantics may differ (see below)

Dedicated vs Hosted behavior (must be clear in docs)
- Hosted: shared capacity, multi-tenant fairness; more likely to use 429 admission control and 503 when breakers open due to regional/model saturation.
- Dedicated: customer-reserved pools; overload is typically customer-driven (burst jobs, concurrency spikes). We should:
  - Provide clear errors (same schema) but tune defaults to avoid surprising shedding.
  - Emphasize autoscaling configuration and recommended concurrency.
  - SLA language may differ; coordinate with Lauren Bishop for final copy.

Proposed changelog entry (public)
Title
“Improved overload behavior for Hosted API (consistent 429/503 + Retry-After)”

Body
“We’ve added layered overload protection to Redwood Hosted API to prevent cascading failures during extreme traffic spikes. When capacity is constrained, requests may fail fast with consistent overload responses (429/503), stable Redwood error codes, and Retry-After guidance—reducing ambiguous timeouts and improving platform stability. See docs for recommended retry patterns and streaming guidance.”

Docs update checklist (public + internal)
Owner: Wei Chen (writer), Elliot Price (program)
- Public docs pages:
  - Overload errors: codes, meanings, example payloads, headers
  - Retry guidance: exponential backoff with jitter, respecting Retry-After
  - Streaming: how to handle disconnects, idempotency guidance, safe retry
  - Hosted vs Dedicated: what differs and why
- Internal docs:
  - Support runbook / macros
  - Incident runbook references (what is “expected shedding” vs incident)

Support readiness checklist
Owner: Dev Patel (Support readiness), Rafael Mendes (SRE), Sean Gallagher (final approval)
Before expanding beyond canary:
- [ ] Zendesk/Jira macros prepared for 429/503 overload explanation
- [ ] “How to read Retry-After” guidance ready
- [ ] Escalation path documented (what data to request from customer: request IDs, timestamps, region, model, SDK version)
- [ ] Known pitfalls documented:
  - Tight retry loops without jitter
  - Double retries (SDK + app)
  - Very high concurrency with long prompts / high max_tokens
  - Streaming clients not handling disconnects gracefully
- [ ] Billing question answer confirmed and consistent across Support + Docs
- [ ] Support training session scheduled (30 min) with example tickets from SUP-3928/SUP-3955

Sales/SE enablement (lightweight)
- One-pager talking points for reliability conversations:
  - Why fail-fast is better than timeouts
  - How Retry-After reduces thundering herds
  - When to recommend Dedicated (predictable sustained throughput)
  - How customers can test their clients (load test w/ backoff + jitter)

Status page / comms guidance
Owner: Nora Ahmed (Status/Transparency), Rafael Mendes (SRE)
When shedding is active and customer-impacting, we should:
- Prefer “Degraded performance / elevated error rates for Hosted API in <region> for <model set>”
- Include what customers can do:
  - Retry with backoff; respect Retry-After
  - If multi-region configured, consider temporarily routing to alternate region
- Avoid overly technical details (e.g., “KV cache thrash”) on public status updates.

Proposed status update template snippet
“We are observing elevated overload responses (429/503) for Redwood Hosted API in <region> affecting <models/routes>. Our overload protection is actively shedding traffic to maintain stability. Clients should respect the Retry-After header and use exponential backoff with jitter. We are adding capacity and expect recovery by <ETA>.”

Observability / internal launch monitoring (what we’ll watch)
- Shed rate by region/model/tier
- Breaker state transitions (open/half-open/closed) and flapping indicators
- Queue depth / scheduler backpressure signals
- p95/p99 latency for successful requests (ensure we don’t “save” stability by destroying median latency)
- Timeout rate and internal 5xx (should go down)
- Top customer support tickets / keywords after change (“429 unexpected”, “stream disconnect”, “Retry-After unclear”)

Known risks and mitigations
1) Retry storms
- Risk: customers see 429/503 and immediately retry in tight loops; load increases.
- Mitigation:
  - Retry-After header + clear docs + SDK helpers
  - Support macros that explicitly mention jitter and disabling stacked retries

2) Breaker flapping
- Risk: oscillation makes experience noisy.
- Mitigation: hysteresis + cooldown; extend canary window if needed; alert tuning after first week.

3) Streaming disconnect experience
- Risk: customers interpret disconnects as “random.”
- Mitigation: docs with explicit guidance; ensure error code is surfaced where possible; improve SDK exceptions.

4) Confusion with quota/rate limit
- Risk: customers believe Redwood introduced new rate limits.
- Mitigation: consistent wording: “overload protection” vs “rate limiting.”

Open questions (need answers before GA wording)
- Billing policy statement for partial work / streaming disconnects (Cole Summers to confirm)
- Exact public list of Redwood overload reason codes (Brian Murphy + Docs)
- Dedicated copy finalization: which behaviors differ and what we promise in SLA language (Lauren Bishop)
- Do we want an opt-out toggle for specific enterprise Hosted customers during the first month? (SRE generally prefers no; discuss case-by-case.)

Approvals
- Product owner (Hosted): Nikhil Sharma
- Reliability exec sponsor: Sean Gallagher
- SRE lead: Rafael Mendes
- Docs: Elliot Price
- Support readiness: Dev Patel
- Dedicated alignment: Lauren Bishop

Next steps (Jan)
- Finalize changelog + docs wording; publish docs alongside staged rollout expansion.
- Run support training + provide macros.
- Confirm billing language and add to FAQ.
- After us-east canary success: expand to next region/model set and update internal comms.
